Part I. Reading passage

Read the story for meaning, decisions and life experiences. After reading, complete the comprehension and language challenges.

The Future Starts with Today: Leo's Journey of Choices and Opportunities

Every person has dreams, but not everyone knows how to turn them into reality. Leo is a 23-year-old university student who believes that success depends on determination, preparation, and the decisions people make every day. He studies English and business administration, works part-time at a local company, and dreams of becoming an international entrepreneur.

Every morning, Leo wakes up at six o'clock and reviews his goals before going to university. He usually studies for two hours after class because he understands that knowledge creates opportunities. At the moment, he is preparing for an important English examination, and he is also developing a business project with his classmates. He has already completed several professional courses, and he has been improving his communication skills for the past three years.

However, Leo's journey has not always been easy. When he was younger, he struggled with public speaking and avoided participating in classroom discussions. One afternoon, while he was presenting a project, he suddenly forgot what he wanted to say. His classmates were watching him, and he felt extremely nervous. By the time his teacher encouraged him to continue, he had already lost his confidence. In fact, he had been worrying about making mistakes for several weeks before that presentation.

Instead of giving up, Leo decided to change his attitude. He realized that mistakes were part of learning and that confidence developed through practice. His teacher explained, "If you practice regularly, you become more confident." Leo understood that if people avoid challenges, they limit their opportunities.

Since that experience, Leo has changed the way he approaches difficulties. He now asks questions, participates in discussions, and practices speaking English whenever possible. He believes that if he continues working hard, he will achieve his professional goals. He also knows that if he doesn't manage his time carefully, he will struggle to balance his studies and personal responsibilities.

Last month, Leo received an invitation to participate in an international entrepreneurship competition. Although he was excited, he was also worried about his English proficiency. He thought, "If I spoke English more fluently, I would feel more comfortable presenting my ideas to international judges." He also imagined that if he had more financial resources, he would invest in better equipment for his project.

Nevertheless, Leo decided not to wait for perfect circumstances. Next month, he will travel to another city to present his business proposal. At this time next month, he will be speaking in front of an international audience. Before the competition begins, he will have completed all the necessary preparations, and by the end of the year, he will have been working on his project for eighteen months.

His friends often ask him whether he is afraid of failing. Leo usually answers, "Of course I am, but fear doesn't have to control my decisions. If I make a mistake, I learn something valuable. If I receive constructive criticism, I will use it to improve my performance. If I were afraid of every possible failure, I would never try anything new."

Leo understands that success is not simply about earning money or receiving recognition. It is about becoming a better person, helping others, and making meaningful contributions to society. He has learned that opportunities do not always appear at the perfect moment. Sometimes people must create them through effort, creativity, and persistence.

As he looks toward the future, Leo remembers the difficulties he has overcome and the lessons he has learned. He knows that he cannot control every situation, but he can control his attitude and his actions. His personal philosophy is simple: "If you want a different future, you must start making different decisions today."

Part X. Speaking — Real-Life Challenges

Instructions: Answer all 10 questions in English (5 academic and 5 personal). For each question: (1) listen carefully, (2) take 5–10 seconds to think, (3) record a 30–45-second answer, (4) explain your opinion or experience, (5) give a reason and a real example. Speak in complete sentences. Do not read a prepared script.

How to organize your answer / Cómo responder:
  1. Answer directly: “I think…” / “I would…” / “Once, I…”
  2. Explain why: “because…” / “The main reason is…”
  3. Give an example: “For example…” / “Last semester…”
  4. Finish your idea: “That's why…” / “So I would…”

These are speaking prompts, not answers to memorize. Use appropriate verb tenses and conditionals; focus on clear pronunciation, connected speech and natural rhythm.
